chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him) regarding the meaning of the killing of Uthman
[And it is a verdict/judgment by him against Uthman and against the people for what they did, and an acquittal of him from his blood]

key_terms.بَرَاءَةٌ: Acquittal, freedom from guilt, or innocence
key_terms.دَمِهِ: His blood (referring to the victim of the assassination)
key_terms.عُثْمَانَ: Uthman ibn Affan, the third Rashidun Caliph

ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's verdict on the assassination of Uthman ibn Affan?
ai.summary: In this nuanced verdict, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the culpability of Uthman for his own mismanagement and the legitimacy of the rebels, declaring his blood 'free of guilt' (bara'ah) to indicate that the killers were not executing an unjust murder but rather carrying out a justified retribution. This statement reflects the Shia scholarly view that Ali’s judgment was based on the specific actions of each party rather than a blanket condemnation, thereby validating the assassins' claim while holding Uthman accountable for his errors.
